# Ship post-release branch cleanup fails non-deterministically (shared /tmp report path / concurrent agents)

## Problem statement

The ship skill's post-release branch cleanup (`runPostReleaseCleanup` in
`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`) fails non-deterministically in a
multi-agent (herdr) environment because it reads and writes a **fixed shared
temp path** (`${os.tmpdir()}/cleanup-summary.json`): when two release/cleanup
processes run concurrently, one clobbers the other's report, so the run logs
"Failed to read summarize report; skipping local cleanup.", then silently
reports "Found 0 merged local branch(es)" and "Pruned 0 local branch(es)" as
if the repository were clean, and the follow-on remote prune also fails.
Observed during the AI_Hell v0.1.10 dev→main release; the same scripts succeed
when re-run standalone.

## Users

- **Agents (Map / herdr):** run automated releases and must not be misled by a
  false "clean" cleanup results.
- **Operators:** trust that post-release cleanup either happened or produced an
  actionable, non-silent warning.
- **Other projects consuming the shared ship/cleanup skills** (AI_Hell, etc.):
  any project can hit the race when releases coincide.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-release cleanup uses a **unique temp path per run** (e.g. derived from
   `mkdtempSync`) for the summarize report; a unit test with two
   concurrent-invocation fakes proves no shared-path clobber.
2. A failed `summarize_branches.py` run or report read no longer silently
   reports "0 merged branches" as if the repo were clean — it logs a distinct,
   actionable warning naming the deterministic remediation (unique temp path).
3. The cleanup stays **non-blocking**: a cleanup failure never changes the
   release exit code (existing AC3 preserved).
4. A transient failure (summarize run / report read / remote prune) is
   **retried once** before the actionable warning is emitted.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the **SorraAgents** repo (ship/cleanup skills are symlinked
  from `~/.pi/agent/skills` into `SorraAgents/skill/`); AI_Hell does not vendor
  these files.
- Cleanup scripts' standalone behaviour (`summarize_branches.py`,
  `prune_local_branches.py`, `delete_remote_branches.py`) must not change.
- Non-blocking guarantee must be preserved (existing AC3 of
  SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG).
- Tests run under `node --test "tests/unit/**/*.mjs"` in SorraAgents.

## Existing state

`runPostReleaseCleanup` passes a fixed `${tempDir}/cleanup-summary.json` to
`summarize_branches.py --report` (~L1110) and reads it back (~L1135). On read
failure it sets `reportData = { branches: [] }` and logs only the generic
"skipping local cleanup" warning, then proceeds to report "Found 0 merged local
branch(es)". The branches-to-delete file already uses `mkdtempSync`
(`cleanup-branches-*`), so only the report path is shared.

## Desired change

- Derive a unique report path per run (mkdtemp-based) used for both the
  `--report` argument and the read-back, so concurrent runs cannot clobber.
- Distinguish a real "no merged branches" result from a failed enumerate/read:
  log an actionable warning (unique-path remediation) instead of the misleading
  "0 merged branches".
- Add a single retry with small backoff for the transient step(s) before
  emitting the warning, preserving non-blocking behaviour.
- Extend `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` with the concurrency-clobber
  test and report-failure-warning test.

## Key Files:

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `runPostReleaseCleanup` (report path
  L1110/L1135, retry logic, warning text)
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` — new AC1 concurrency fake test,
  AC2 warning test, AC4 retry test

## Risks & assumptions

- **Retry must not mask real errors** — the single retry is for transient
  failures only; the actionable warning must still be emitted on the second
  failure (assumption: failures are quiet enough to retry once without
  doubling wall-clock time; mitigation: small backoff).
- **Scope creep** — deeper cleanup-skill refactoring, branch-deletion policy
  changes, or fixing `delete_remote_branches.py`/`summarize_branches.py`
  behaviour are out of scope; if such work is discovered, record it as new
  linked work items (not here).
- **Test isolation** — the concurrency test must not touch the real
  `/tmp/cleanup-summary.json` or run real git commands; fakes only
  (assumption: existing `setupRunReleaseFixture` harness is reused/adapted).
- **Cross-repo tracking** — item originated in the AI_Hell worklog
  (AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU, moved here per producer decision Q1c); AI_Hell leaves
  no orphan reference after deletion.
- **Non-blocking guarantee** — AC3 must survive the retry addition; the retry
  must also be non-blocking.

## Related work

- SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG — Automate post-release cleanup (introduced this code).
- AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ — Discord notification fails (precedent: ship-skill bug
  tracked in AH worklog, fixed in SorraAgents).
- SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH — Live-repo guard concurrency (related concurrency issue).
- SA-0MUJQ5BPF001PICU — Test-suite flakiness under concurrent agent load.
- discovered-from: AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU (moved from AI_Hell worklog);
  discovered-from: release-v0.1.10.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should the fix be implemented/tracked? The code lives in
  SorraAgents (ship/cleanup skills); this item is tracked in the AI_Hell
  worklog." — Answer (producer): **(c)** "check an equivalent doesn't already
  exist first, delete this item" (i.e. move the item entirely to SorraAgents).
  Source: interactive reply. Research: searched the SorraAgents worklog for
  `cleanup-summary`, `runPostReleaseCleanup`, `post-release cleanup`, `tmp
  path`, `shared report`, `concurrent agents`, `branch cleanup` — no equivalent
  open/closed item; only the completed feature SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG and two
  unrelated concurrency items. Outcome: created SA-0MV6JQP9K004QGUT here and
  deleted AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU.
- Q2: "Is 'retry once' in scope? Expected Behaviour promises it but the ACs do
  not require it." — Answer (producer): **(a)** add it as AC4. Source:
  interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MS3ATINN006QT1M** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/cleanup/scripts/inspect_current_branch.py:28 — Do not catch blind exception: `Exception` (BLE001) (completed)
- **SA-0MS3ATJR7003CK2B** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/cleanup/scripts/prune_local_branches.py:38 — Do not catch blind exception: `Exception` (BLE001) (completed)
- **SA-0MSMT0B3E009NTB7** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_cleanup_scripts.py:1 — Import block is un-sorted or un-formatted (I001) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+162 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+154 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance, actionable (+144 more)

## Impact

A release or cleanup run can no longer be misled into reporting a clean repository when its branch-enumeration report was clobbered by another concurrent run: each run now owns a unique report path, transient failures are retried once, and any remaining failure produces an actionable warning naming the remediation instead of a false "0 merged branches".

> **Migrated from the `llm` worklog:** this item was originally filed there as `LP-0MVF4OPC1001RYX6` (deleted after migration on 2026-10-20). The `llm` repo remains the sweep target for its markers listed below; all skill-code changes live here in `SorraAgents`.

# Remove stale REFACTOR markers when their work item closes

## Problem statement

The refactor skill injects `REFACTOR-<id>` marker comments into source files to suppress duplicate work-item creation, but there is no removal path: once the referenced smell is fixed (or judged a false positive) and its work item closes, the marker persists and — because `has_existing_comment(file_path, smell_type)` matches on *smell type* only — permanently suppresses detection of that smell type in that file.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `/skill:refactor` or the implement pipeline's refactor step — they trust duplicate suppression to be accurate; a stale marker silently hides a real regression.
- **Developers reading source files** — stale markers are noise that misrepresents outstanding work.
- **Producers triaging the Refactor backlog** — a closed work item should leave no trace in the codebase.

Example user stories:

- "As an agent running the refactor step, when a marker's work item is already closed, I want the marker gone (or ignored) so I do not skip a smell that has regressed."
- "As a developer, when a refactor item is completed or judged a false positive, I want its comment removed from the file without touching surrounding code or line endings."
- "As a producer, I want a single command that reports every stale marker in the project and can clean them up."

## Existing state

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` provides `inject_refactor_comment()`, `has_existing_comment()`, `get_comment_style()` and `_build_comment_block()`; there is **no removal function**.
- Two slightly different regexes parse markers: `comment_injection.REFACTOR_PATTERN` (`REFACTOR-(\S+).*?smell:\s*(\S+)`, DOTALL) and `workitem_creation.REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN` (multi-line, expects a comment prefix before `smell:`).
- Markers are written in two shapes: line-prefixed (`# <!-- REFACTOR-…` … `# -->` for Python/YAML/shell, `// <!-- …` for JS/TS) and native block (`<!-- … -->` for Markdown/HTML). CSS-family files use `/* … */` with ` * ` prefixes.
- `inject_refactor_comment()` reads and writes text mode without `newline=""`, so injected files are normalised; removal must not repeat that mistake.
- `StatusLifecycle.show()` and `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags()` already provide safe work-item lookup and prefix-to-sibling worklog-store resolution. Verified: a bare `wl show <foreign-prefix-id>` fails ("Work item not found"), so a sweep **must** inject `--worklog-dir` from the shared resolver.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` `remediate_pre_existing()` injects markers only for smells it just filed items for; the pipeline syncs the worklog first (`wl sync --if-idle`) and has no post-close hook.
- The canonical source of the skill is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/` (symlinked into `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor`); its tests live in `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/`, with `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` (1251 lines) covering the current API.
- Stale markers confirmed at HEAD in the `llm` repo (work-item state checked 2026-10-20):

| File | Marker | Item stage |
|---|---|---|
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` | open / `intake_complete` — reported false positive |
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:8` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTV87EC4006EU5Z` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTRWI65I005VXOC` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/provider.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MSI4ZIF60064EOR` | completed / `done` |

- The same defect is visible in the `SorraAgents` repo itself: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (2 markers), `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` (3), `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (2), `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_regressions.py` — 4 of these reference `completed` items, the rest reference `open / idea` items.

## Desired change

1. **Removal API** in `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`: `remove_refactor_marker(file_path, work_item_id) -> dict` (or a small dataclass) that locates the whole marker block for that id — line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes — and deletes it, leaving the remainder of the file byte-identical (including CRLF/LF and the file's original trailing newline). Absent marker → `{"removed": False, "reason": "absent"}`; repeated runs are no-ops.
2. **Sweep module** (new `skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py`): discover markers in repo-tracked files (exclude `.worklog/`, `node_modules`, binaries), group by referenced work-item id to one `wl show` per distinct id (worklog dir resolved via `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags`), classify each marker as `stale` (stage `in_review`/`done`/`completed` or status `completed`), `active` (any other resolved stage) or `unknown` (lookup failed), and return a structured report.
3. **Trigger** from the refactor pipeline: run the sweep after the `wl sync` and **before** smell detection, so `has_existing_comment` never observes a stale marker. Non-fatal on `wl` failure (log a warning, keep markers). Standalone CLI entry point (`--sweep-markers`, report-only by default, `--apply` to delete) and a skip flag (`--no-marker-sweep`).
4. **`has_existing_comment` correctness**: keep it a pure file predicate by default, but accept an optional `is_active` resolver/callback so a caller can exclude terminal items; the pipeline's sweep-before-detect ordering is what makes the default path correct. `unknown` markers keep suppressing (conservative) and are reported as warnings.
5. **False-positive path**: a marker whose item is still open but was judged a false positive must be removable explicitly (`--remove-marker <work-item-id>` or `remove_refactor_marker()` called directly), independent of item stage.
6. **Unit tests** in `tests/test_refactor/`: removal for `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes; block and line-prefix styles; CRLF preservation; absent-marker no-op; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file touching only the target block; classification of `in_review`/`done`/`completed`/`open`; `unknown` id kept and reported; dry-run performs no writes; cross-store id resolution.
7. **Sweep the existing stale markers** in `llm` (6 stale; the false positive needs an explicit decision) and in `SorraAgents` (4 stale), so `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` afterwards shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
8. **Documentation**: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (§ REFACTOR Comments + flags table + report keys), `docs/refactor.md` (§ 4 Work Item Creation, troubleshooting "Duplicate work items created", module reference), and module docstrings. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (ship pipeline owns it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `remove_refactor_marker()` removes a `REFACTOR-<id>` marker block (line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles) from a file while leaving all surrounding content byte-identical and preserving the file's line endings (verified by a CRLF fixture test).
- [ ] Removal is a no-op (`removed=False`) when the marker is absent, and re-running it is idempotent.
- [ ] A sweep reports every marker in the project with its referenced item's stage and a classification of `stale` / `active` / `unknown`; removal is triggered for markers whose work item is at a terminal stage (`in_review`, `done`, `completed`).
- [ ] Sweep work-item lookups resolve the correct worklog store via the shared resolver (a foreign-prefix id resolves; failure is non-fatal and keeps the marker as `unknown`).
- [ ] `has_existing_comment()` no longer suppresses detection for closed work items — covered by a test asserting a terminal-stage marker is not treated as an existing comment on the sweep-before-detect path (and via the optional active-item filter).
- [ ] An explicit false-positive removal path exists for markers whose work item is still open, with `--dry-run` making no writes.
- [ ] Running the sweep (apply mode) removes the 6 stale `llm` markers listed above and the 4 stale `SorraAgents` markers; a follow-up `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles; absent marker; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file; terminal vs non-terminal classification; unknown id; dry-run no-write.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Canonical source is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/`; never edit `~/.pi/agent/skills/...` (the installer replaces it) and never hand-edit markers in `llm` outside an authorised implementation run.
- Standard library only — no new third-party dependencies.
- One `wl show` per distinct referenced work-item id (cached per run); the sweep must stay in the same sub-second-to-low-seconds envelope as the existing pipeline rather than spawning per marker.
- Sweep is read-only unless `--apply` (or the default pipeline policy) removes stale markers; `--dry-run` must never write.
- Never remove a marker for an item that is not terminal unless explicitly requested by id.
- Only scan git-tracked files in the repo root (skip `.worklog/`, worktrees, `node_modules`, binary files).
- Work-item ids may belong to sibling project stores; always route `wl` through the shared resolver, not the cwd default.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — add `remove_refactor_marker()`, a single tolerant marker parser covering both existing regexes, `is_active` filter hook on `has_existing_comment()`, and `newline=""` IO.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py` (new) — marker discovery, per-id work-item lookup via `shared.status_lifecycle`, classification and report structure.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — sweep step after `wl sync` / before detection, `--sweep-markers`, `--apply`, `--remove-marker`, `--no-marker-sweep` flags, report keys.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — reuse the unified marker pattern instead of its own `REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN`.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — marker lifecycle and new flags.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/docs/refactor.md` — § 4, troubleshooting, module reference.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — extend with removal tests.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_marker_sweep.py` (new) — sweep classification, dry-run, unknown ids, non-fatal wl failures.
- `llm`: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py`, `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — sweep targets only (no hand edits).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Repository placement (assumption A1):** the skill's source of truth is `SorraAgents`, so the code change belongs here (this `SA-` item) and owns the `llm` marker sweep alongside the `SorraAgents` sweep; Q1 is resolved by this migration.
- **No close hook:** `wl` exposes no plugin/hook on close (only `wl plugins` for discovery), so "triggered when the item reaches a terminal stage" is implemented as a sweep at refactor-run time plus a standalone command — not an event. Assumption A2.
- **False-positive regression loop:** removing the marker for a closed false-positive item re-enables detection, so the next scan re-files the same item. Mitigation: false positives must be closed with a reason *and* either fixed or excluded via `.refactor.json`/per-file ignore; the sweep should report (not silently hide) this case. Scope-creep risk — an ignore-list mechanism is a separate work item.
- **Mixed answers to `unknown`:** unresolvable ids (deleted items, wrong store) could hide real work. Conservative default: keep + warn.
- **Formatting churn:** a naive implementation strips a leading blank line or rewrites CRLF files, producing whole-file diffs. Byte-preserving IO (`newline=""`, explicit trailing-newline handling) plus a CRLF fixture test is mandatory.
- **Regex divergence:** the two existing patterns disagree on block styles; unifying them is required or Markdown/CSS markers will be missed by the sweep.
- **Scope creep:** generalising to a lifecycle framework for all agent-injected comments is out of scope; record as a separate item if it surfaces.

## Open questions

1. **Repository and work-item placement** — ~~implement in `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor` under a new `SA-` item (this `LP-` item keeps the `llm` sweep and records the blocker), or keep everything under this `LP-` item and treat the SorraAgents edits as out-of-worktree?~~ **RESOLVED** by migration: this `SA-` item hosts the skill change; the `llm` marker list below stays the sweep target.
2. **Trigger surface** — sweep automatically inside the refactor pipeline (default) plus a standalone `--sweep-markers --apply`, or standalone-only (manual/cron)?
3. **False positives and unresolvable ids** — should `has_existing_comment` keep suppressing on `unknown` ids (conservative) while a manual `--remove-marker <id>` handles false positives, or should both be dropped automatically?

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which repository should host the skill change — `SorraAgents/skill/refactor` (canonical source, its own `SA-` item) or this `LP-` item in `llm`? (moot — item migrated to `SorraAgents` as `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9`)" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor`; the skill's tests live in `SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/`; `implement.py` creates worktrees from the cwd's `.worklog`, so an `LP-` item cannot legally host edits under `SorraAgents`. **Recommended:** new `SA-` item in `SorraAgents` for the skill change, `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9` scoped to the `llm` marker sweep and recording the blocker.
- Q: "How should the terminal-stage trigger be implemented, given `wl` exposes no close hook?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: `wl plugins` only lists plugins; no event/hook surface found; the refactor pipeline already runs at the end of implementation and syncs first. **Recommended:** sweep inside the refactor pipeline (after `wl sync`, before detection) plus a standalone `--sweep-markers` report/`--apply` CLI.
- Q: "Should markers referencing unresolvable work items, and false-positive markers whose item is still open, be removed automatically?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: all `llm` markers resolve today except none; `LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` is open at `intake_complete` while the marker is documented as a false positive. **Recommended:** keep `unknown` markers and warn; require an explicit `--remove-marker <id>` for open-item false positives.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE** – Refactor: Formatting in a test file of the (since-deleted) `proxy-usage-analysis` skill (open)
- **LP-0MQ5NI704006WINH** – Unit tests: cooldown behavior (completed)
- **LP-0MROYEVL3004Y04Z** – Manually fix remaining 5 non-auto-fixable lint errors (4 F401, 1 F811) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absent, accept, acceptance, accurate, active (+400 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absent, accept, acceptance, accurate, active (+400 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: absent, accept, acceptance, accurate, active (+400 more)

data.description:
## Objective

Make `/skill:ship release` judge the importance of the work items in the release and propose the semantically correct semver bump (patch, minor, or major), instead of always bumping patch — with the producer asked in the PI session before any non-patch bump is applied.

## Problem Statement

The ship skill currently always increments the `z` (patch) component of the release version (`merge-dev-to-main.sh` defaults `BUMP="patch"`), even when the release adds new or breaking capability. Releases that add features therefore ship as patch versions (e.g. `v0.1.19` instead of `v0.2.0`), misrepresenting the release's impact and forcing the producer to remember `--bump minor` manually.

## Users

- **Release manager (the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`)** — must judge the release's importance from the items being shipped and propose the right bump without extra flags.
- **Producer** — must see and approve any non-patch bump, in the session, with a full justification naming the items that triggered it.

Example user stories:

- As a release manager, when every item in the release is a fix, chore, or documentation change, I want the release to bump patch automatically so that I don't have to think about semver.
- As a release manager, when the release contains meaningful new capability, I want to propose a minor bump with evidence, rather than silently shipping it as a patch.
- As a producer, I want to be asked, in the session, before a minor or major bump is applied, with a justification naming the items and why they warrant the bump — and I want to be able to decline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- The agent judges the importance of the release from those items and proposes exactly one bump: **patch** when the release only fixes, documents, or maintains; **minor** when it adds meaningful new capability; **major** when it breaks or removes existing capability or otherwise changes behaviour incompatibly (the existing `--bump` override remains available).
- A **patch** proposal proceeds automatically with no producer interaction — the current `--bump patch` behaviour and `merge-dev-to-main.sh` default are unchanged.
- A **minor or major** proposal prints a full justification — each contributing item ID and title, why it warrants the bump, and the proposed `old → new` version — and the agent asks the producer **in the PI session**; no git mutation, tag, PR, or worklog close occurs until the producer approves.
- Producer approval proceeds with the approved `--bump`; a declined non-patch proposal is honoured (the agent does not apply it, and records the decision and the producer's preferred bump in the session and on the release's work item).
- In a non-interactive/headless context where the producer cannot be asked, a minor or major proposal is never auto-approved: the agent records the justification, flags the item for producer review, and stops.
- The judgement is based on the release items' content (Impact/description/capability), not on `issueType` or a label lookup; the justification cites the evidence used.
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics rather than duplicating version arithmetic.
- Unit tests cover: candidate gathering (including an empty candidate set), the review packet/justification rendering, patch auto-proceed, and the non-patch approval-pending behaviour (no mutation); no test reads or mutates the live worklog.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, and code comments.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Releases that add or break capability will carry a version number that reflects it, and producers will be asked in-session to approve that call with evidence instead of policing `--bump` flags by hand.

## Existing State

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` sets `BUMP="patch"` by default and accepts `--bump patch|minor|major` (already validates the value).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` parses and forwards `--bump` to the merge script; the wrapper has no bump evaluation step and its documented exit codes are `0`–`14`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` already implements `patch`/`minor`/`major` arithmetic correctly (including `z = 0` on minor and `y = z = 0` on major) and resolves `package.json` or `pyproject.toml` as the version source.
- Release candidates are items with `stage: in_review` (`check-audit-gate.js::getCandidateItems`), so the candidate set already exists.
- The release wrapper subprocess is non-interactive, but the ship skill itself is a PI skill executed by an agent in a session — the agent, not the shell script, is the component that can ask the producer.

## Desired Change

1. Add a small, unit-testable helper (e.g. `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js`) that gathers release candidates and renders a compact review packet: per item `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, `## Impact` (or user story) and a truncated description excerpt, plus the current version and the three candidate bump outcomes. It gathers and renders only — no judgement, no mutation.
2. Add a "Version bump evaluation" step at the start of the documented release workflow in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (before gates and merge): run the preflight, judge the release's importance, and choose patch/minor/major.
3. Patch → run the release normally (patch is the existing default).
4. Minor/major → present the justification to the producer in the session and wait for approval; on approval run `run-release.js --bump <approved>`; on decline, do not apply.
5. Keep the judgement rationale and the producer's decision in the session output and, where the release is tied to a work item, in a comment so the version choice is auditable.
6. Update `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and the SKILL.md workflow/argument docs to describe the evaluation step and the in-session approval gate.

## Constraints

- **Judgement stays with the agent:** no issue-type or label mapping, and no mechanical classifier is added — the evaluation prompt/rubric is documented, and the agent makes the call from the items' content.
- **Producer gates non-patch bumps:** minor and major bumps must never be applied without an explicit producer approval in the session. Patch bumps stay automatic.
- **Fail-closed in headless runs:** where no producer is available (downtime/automated dispatches), a minor/major proposal must stop with producer review rather than self-approve.
- **Backward compatible:** an explicit `--bump` keeps its current meaning and precedence; invoking `merge-dev-to-main.sh` directly keeps its `patch` default.
- **No duplicated version arithmetic:** reuse `bump-version.js` for the actual bump; the new code only gathers evidence and renders the proposal.
- **Fail-safe:** an unreadable/empty candidate set must default to patch with a warning and must never block a release that would otherwise succeed; a preflight failure must not mutate the repository.
- **No live-worklog test access:** unit tests must inject the candidate-fetch boundary.
- **Auditability:** the proposed and approved bump, the justification, and the producer's decision are recorded (session output plus a work-item comment for item-linked releases).

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — new "Version bump evaluation" workflow step, in-session approval gate, argument/behaviour docs.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` — new candidate-gathering/review-packet helper (and its tests).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — unchanged `--bump` forwarding, plus any logging of the decided bump; verify no new git side effects.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — receives the decided `--bump`; default unchanged.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` — reused as-is for arithmetic (verify minor resets patch to `0`, major resets minor and patch).
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getCandidateItems` is the release-candidate source.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — reference for the evaluation step and approval gate.
- `skill/ship/tests/` — new unit tests for the preflight helper and the approval-pending path.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** — Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (introduced the bump step and `v<semver>` tag convention).
- **SA-0MVN2B0DJ00135W0** — ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (version source resolution).
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** — Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs.
- **SA-0MQI6MDUP001S8NL** — bump-version.js isMainModule check fails on symlinked install paths.
- **SA-0MRGVN9XM003LNQ7** — Close work items when shipping (uses the released version in `Shipped in v<version>` markers).
- **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** — Newly-created-tag gate (precedent for a fail-closed startup gate with a distinct exit code).
- **SA-0MUIVIJFT0009ZNV** — Missing-script fail-fast (precedent for refusing early, before any git/worklog side effects).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Judgement subjectivity (risk):** "meaningful new capability" is a judgement call, and two agents could judge the same release differently. Mitigation: a documented rubric (new capability → minor, breaking change → major, fixes/docs/maintenance only → patch), the evidence-based justification, and the producer's in-session approval for every non-patch bump.
- **Producer availability (risk):** a headless release cannot ask anyone. Mitigation: a non-patch proposal in a headless run stops with producer review instead of self-approving; patch releases are unaffected.
- **Agent discipline (risk):** the gate lives in the documented workflow, so a release run by bypassing the skill (direct `run-release.js`) is not gated. Mitigation: document the workflow as the canonical path, and keep the version arithmetic and safety gates in the script unchanged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-item bump annotations, automatic CHANGELOG grouping, and mechanical classification are separate opportunities and should be filed as follow-up items rather than folded into this change.
- **Empty candidate set:** a release with no `in_review` items (e.g. hotfix) defaults to patch and logs why.
- **`--skip-checks` interaction (assumption):** `--skip-checks` bypasses branch/critical gates only; the bump evaluation still runs, and an explicit `--bump` remains an operator override.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (basis for minor-worthiness):** How should the release's importance be judged?
  - Options considered: (A) by `issueType`; (B) by `priority`; (C) by an explicit label/tag; (D) the agent's interpretation of the items' importance.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's not about issue type or label. It's about your interpretation of the importance of the items in the release. Make the best call you can. Check with the producer." → **Option D**, with a documented rubric and producer confirmation.
- **Q2 (approval mechanism):** How is the producer asked to approve a proposed minor/major bump?
  - Options considered: (A) fail-closed exit code + producer re-runs with `--bump`; (B) an interactive prompt inside the PI session; (C) automatic bump with a warning.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's a skill in PI, ask in the session." → **Option B**: the agent presents the justification and asks the producer in the session; the subprocess itself stays non-interactive.
- **Q3 (major inference):** Should a `major` (x) bump be inferred?
  - Options considered: (A) no — only minor/patch; (B) infer and suggest major, but never apply without producer approval.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "You can infer it and suggest it, but never implement without checking with the producer." → **Option B**: major may be proposed and justified, gated by the same in-session producer approval as minor.

## Objective

Add the **Version bump evaluation** step to the ship skill's documented release workflow and implement the **in-session producer approval gate** for non-patch bumps. This is the agent-behaviour half of the feature: the preflight helper (sibling child) supplies evidence; this child defines the rubric, the patch auto-proceed path, and the minor/major approval-pending contract.

## User Story

As a producer, I want to be asked, in the PI session, before a minor or major bump is applied — with a justification naming the items and why they warrant it — and I want to be able to decline, so that releases carry a version that honestly reflects their impact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` gains a startup **"Version bump evaluation"** step, placed **before** the gating checks and any git mutation, which runs the preflight, states the judgement rubric, and chooses exactly one bump: **patch** (fixes/docs/maintenance only), **minor** (meaningful new capability), **major** (breaking/removed/incompatible behaviour).
- The rubric is content-based (Impact/user story/description/capability), **not** an `issueType` or label mapping; the written justification cites the evidence used (each contributing item id + title and why).
- The agent judges the importance of the release from those items and proposes exactly one bump: **patch** when the release only fixes, documents, or maintains; **minor** when it adds meaningful new capability; **major** when it breaks or removes existing capability or otherwise changes behaviour incompatibly (the existing `--bump` override remains available).
- **Patch** proceeds automatically with no producer interaction; `merge-dev-to-main.sh`'s `patch` default and `run-release.js --bump patch` behaviour are unchanged.
- **Minor/major** prints a full justification — each contributing item id and title, the reason, and the proposed `old → new` version — and the agent asks the producer **in the PI session**. No git mutation, tag, PR, or worklog close occurs until the producer approves; approval runs `run-release.js --bump <approved>`.
- A **declined** non-patch proposal is honoured: the bump is not applied; the decision and the producer's preferred bump are recorded in the session output and on the release's work item (comment) where one exists.
- **Headless/fail-closed:** where no producer is available (downtime/automated dispatch), a minor/major proposal is never auto-approved — the agent records the justification, sets the release work item `needsProducerReview` (or comments + stops when there is no release item), and stops.
- The existing explicit `--bump` keeps its meaning and precedence as an operator override; `--skip-checks` does not bypass the evaluation or its approval gate.
- Unit tests cover: candidate gathering (including an empty candidate set), the review packet/justification rendering, patch auto-proceed, and the non-patch approval-pending behaviour (no mutation); no test reads or mutates the live worklog.
- Node tests (`skill/ship/tests/`) pin the workflow contract: SKILL.md documents the evaluation step and the in-session approval gate; the approval-pending path performs **no** mutation (no merge script invocation, no `wl close`). Tests are hermetic.
- `run_tests.py --scope changed` passes.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the failing workflow-contract test first (e.g. `test_bump_evaluation_workflow.mjs`) asserting the SKILL.md section + approval-pending no-mutation contract.
2. Add the "Version bump evaluation" section to `skill/ship/SKILL.md` before the Gating section, including the rubric, patch/minor/major rules, the in-session ask, decline handling, headless fail-closed behaviour, and auditability.
3. Update the `Usage`/`--bump` documentation and the `Release Process` step list to show evaluation as step 0/0.5 (before gates), noting `--bump` override precedence.
4. Document the approval-pending contract as agent behaviour (the subprocess stays non-interactive) so there is no mechanical classifier.
5. Add a small, testable decision helper if needed (e.g. `shouldAskProducer(bump)`) to keep the auto-proceed vs approval-pending rule out of prose only; keep it pure.
6. Record the chosen and approved bump with a work-item comment when the release is item-linked (session output for item-exempt releases).

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_evaluation_workflow.mjs` (new)
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` (consume, do not modify arithmetic)
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` (documented `--bump` contract only; no new git side effects)

## Constraints

- Judgement stays with the agent; no mechanical classifier or issue-type mapping.
- Producer gates every minor/major bump; patch stays automatic.
- Fail-closed in headless runs.
- Backward compatible: explicit `--bump` retains precedence; direct `merge-dev-to-main.sh` keeps `patch` default.

## Deliverables

- SKILL.md workflow/argument/behaviour docs + hermetic workflow-contract tests.

Deliver the byte-preserving removal API and a single tolerant marker parser used by both removal and duplicate detection.

## Goal

Add `remove_refactor_marker()` plus one parser that locates every marker style without normalising the file.

## Impact

Developers and agents can delete a stale REFACTOR marker without touching surrounding code or rewriting a file's line endings.

## Context

Parent SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9. Two divergent regexes currently parse markers (`comment_injection.REFACTOR_PATTERN` and `workitem_creation.REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN`); unify them so Markdown/CSS markers are not missed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `remove_refactor_marker()` removes a `REFACTOR-<id>` marker block (line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles) from a file while leaving all surrounding content byte-identical and preserving the file's line endings (verified by a CRLF fixture test).
- Removal is a no-op (`removed=False`) when the marker is absent, and re-running it is idempotent.
- `has_existing_comment()` no longer suppresses detection for closed work items — covered by a test asserting a terminal-stage marker is not treated as an existing comment on the sweep-before-detect path (and via the optional active-item filter).
- One tolerant marker parser replaces both existing regexes; `workitem_creation.REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN` is rewritten in terms of it.
- File IO uses `newline=""` for read and write, so removal never normalises CRLF; optional ` * ` prefixes in CSS blocks are tolerated.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `remove_refactor_marker(file_path, work_item_id) -> {"removed": bool, "reason": str}` to `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`.
- Add one compiled parser that locates the full block for an id across all four comment styles (line-prefixed and native block, optional ` * ` prefixes).
- Remove exactly the bytes the injector added (leading separator newline when present) and restore the trailing newline exactly.
- Add an optional `is_active: Callable[[str], bool] | None` parameter to `has_existing_comment()`; export the unified pattern for `workitem_creation`.

## Key Files

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py`
- `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py`

## Dependencies

- Depends on "Test: REFACTOR marker removal API".

Add a sweep module that discovers markers in git-tracked files, resolves each referenced work item once via the shared resolver, and returns a structured `stale`/`active`/`unknown` report.

## Goal

Create `skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py` with `discover_markers()` and `sweep_markers()`.

## Impact

Producers and agents get one command that reports every stale marker in the project and can clean them up, instead of grepping and checking worklog state by hand.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A sweep reports every marker in the project with its referenced item's stage and a classification of `stale` / `active` / `unknown`; removal is triggered for markers whose work item is at a terminal stage (`in_review`, `done`, `completed`).

data.description:
Wire the sweep into the refactor pipeline and expose the standalone/CLI controls.

## Goal

Add a sweep step after `wl sync`/before detection, plus `--sweep-markers`, `--apply`, `--remove-marker` and `--no-marker-sweep`.

## Impact

A normal refactor run silently clears stale markers before detection, and an operator can run a report-only sweep or remove a specific false-positive marker from the command line.

## Context

Parent SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9. The JSON report and human output must surface the sweep result so the operator can see what was removed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The pipeline runs the sweep after `wl sync` and before smell detection, so `has_existing_comment` never observes a stale marker.

Test/verification children (C1, C3, C5) precede their implementation children. Each feature is an end-to-end slice (code + tests + docs/report keys). AC coverage review: **proceed** (100%).

## Decisions (Appendix updates)

- **Q2 — Trigger surface — RESOLVED** using the recommended option already encoded in the brief's "Desired change": pipeline sweep after `wl sync` and before smell detection, plus a standalone `--sweep-markers` (report-only) / `--apply` and a `--no-marker-sweep` escape hatch.
- **Q3 — False positives and unresolvable ids — RESOLVED** using the recommended option: `unknown` markers are kept and warned about (conservative); an open-item false positive is removable only via an explicit `--remove-marker <work-item-id>` / `remove_refactor_marker()`.
- **Q1 — Repository placement — already resolved** by migration to this SA- item; all skill code, tests and docs live in `SorraAgents`.

## Related work / overlap (producer decision flagged)

`SA-0MVZA21600087VRD` ("Reap REFACTOR- marker blocks when the recorded smell is fixed", stage `plan_complete`) covers overlapping ground: a removal/reap module, a CLI, tests and docs. It differs in policy — it treats a *missing* work item as stale-and-removable (`work-item-missing`) and keeps the logic out of `comment_injection.py`, whereas this item keeps `unknown` markers conservative and puts `remove_refactor_marker()` in `comment_injection.py`. This item is broader and supersedes it functionally. It is **not** closed here (partial overlap, not a full duplicate); a comment was left on that item recommending the producer close/supersede it to avoid two parallel implementations.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Cross-repo `llm` sweep (C8):** the `llm` markers live in `/home/rgardler/projects/llm`. The SorraAgents worktree cannot commit changes in another repository, so C8 runs the standalone CLI there and records the changes for an authorised `llm` commit; markers are never hand-edited. If the producer declines the cross-repo run, C8 falls back to producing a report/patch for the `llm` producer.
- **False-positive regression loop:** removing a closed false-positive marker re-enables detection, so the next scan re-files the same item. The sweep reports (not silently hides) this case; an ignore-list mechanism is out of scope (separate item).
- **Formatting churn:** byte-preserving IO (`newline=""`) plus a CRLF fixture test is mandatory (C1/C2).
- **Regex divergence:** the two existing patterns disagree on block styles; C2 unifies them so Markdown/CSS markers are not missed.
- **No close hook:** `wl` exposes no close/event hook, so removal is a sweep at refactor-run time plus a standalone command (not an event).

## Plan changelog

- 2026-11-14: Decomposed into C1–C8, wired 9 dependency edges, resolved Q2/Q3 with the brief's recommended options, recorded the `SA-0MVZA21600087VRD` overlap, and ran the AC-coverage review (proceed, 100%).
